member.name: T:Dx.Domain.Invariant
member.summary: Provides assertion‑style invariant enforcement.

remarks.para: Invariants represent structural truths of the domain model. Violating an invariant indicates either a programmer error or a corrupt internal state.
Invariant methods throw exceptions on failure. They are intended for kernel, infrastructure, or otherwise trusted code paths where recovery is neither meaningful nor expected.
For recoverable, flow‑oriented validation that should not throw, use instead.

member.name: T:Dx.Domain.Dx.Require
member.summary: Represents validation-style invariant checks that return failed Results instead of throwing exceptions.

remarks.para: Require represents recoverable domain validation. A failed requirement indicates that an operation cannot proceed, but does not represent a corrupted program state or programming error.
In contrast to , methods on this class never throw as a result of validation failure. All outcomes are expressed as values and are therefore composable, inspectable, and analyzable.
This class is the primary validation surface intended for third-party, application-level, and flow-oriented domain logic.
